newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - DEC 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - DEC 9.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company.
-- FRANCE MAY SPLIT THOMSON IN SELL-OFF

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has indicated that the Thomson electronics and defence group it is attempting to sell off may be split into two units to facilitate the sale. Speaking to the Financial Times, Juppe promised a speedy relaunch of efforts to privatise the company. An attempt last week was derailed after the Privatisation Commission raised objections about the planned sale by bidder Lagardere of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo of South Korea.
-- MARKETS EXPECT CALM TO FOLLOW FRIDAY PRICE SCARE

Analysts are reported to be confident that while U.S. markets may show some volatility when they reopen on Monday, a degree of calm should have returned after Friday's sharp falls, sparked by comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. Analysts had interpreted the comments as indicating he thought the equity market was overvalued. Some observers have welcomed a degree of reality that the comments may have injected.
-- CLUB MED RISKS TAKEOVER AS SHARE PACT ENDS

The end of a six-year shareholder pact that controlled 35 percent of the voting rights in Club Mediterranean has increased the prospects of a possible takeover of the French holiday group. The deal had limited those in the shareholder deal to amassing a 13 percent stake in the company, which has been the target for criticism over its financial performance of late. The Club Med chairman has noted the deal ended as those involved required more freedom at a time of financial market volatility.
-- UNICHEM IN PLAN TO RUN DOCTOR SERVICES FOR NHS

It is reported that the UK pharmaceutical retailer and distributor Unichem is planning to operate family doctor services on behalf of the National Health Service once the forthcoming primary care bill becomes law next year. Unichem hopes to include an insurer, possibly Bupa, in a consortium that would operate one-stop health facilities, and has said it is awaiting guidance on the matter from the Department of Health.
-- BCCI CREDITORS TO RECEIVE 1.35 BILLION DOLLARS PAYOUT

Five years after the collapse of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), it is thought that on Monday its liquidators will pay 25,000 creditors some $1.35 billion. This represents 24.5 percent of the sum lost by creditors in the bank's failure. The final dividend to be paid is expected by the liquidators to reach between 30 and 40 percent of the amounts lost. On Monday, larger claims will be settled electronically, with cheques being despatched to smaller creditors.
-- DOUBT OVER IT TRADE PACT AS EU CALLS FOR WIDER DEAL

Doubts have been raised about the prospects for a WTO accord in the area of international trade in information technology after the EU insisted that such an agreement include several other trade issues. The EU demand, made in advance of a Singapore meeting of trade representatives, has met with criticism from the U.S. that accused it of vacillating. The EU, meanwhile, has noted that the U.S. itself has backed away from reducing tariffs on a range of IT-related products.
-- APPEAL TO KOHL ON STABILITY PACT

Fearing that continued deadlock over the establishment of a post-EMU stability will sour EU relations, France will on Monday call on Germany to modify its position on the issue in time for an agreement to be reached at a forthcoming Dublin summit. To date Germany has been insistent that any such pact be strictly enforced so as to ensure continued budgetary discipline among those states taking part in the single currency.
-- EUROTUNNEL REINTRODUCES LIMITED SHUTTLE SERVICE

On Monday, Eurotunnel is scheduled to resume a limited passenger service through the Channel Tunnel. The continuing effects of November's fire will, however, mean that the service offered will be less than half the tunnel's usual capacity for such traffic. The limits will result in the company being unable to take advantage of a seasonal rise in demand and will also mean that space on passenger shuttles will be prioritised for those who have made prior bookings.
-- C&W BECOMES BIG SPONSOR OF SADLER'S WELLS

In an attempt to turn Sadler's Wells into Britain's most technically advanced theatre, Cable & Wireless plans to provide the London venue with some 440,000 stg in sponsorship over the next four years. Currently being replaced with a more modern building, Sadler's Wells will as part of the C&W deal receive funding for advanced telecoms systems as well as a computer controlled rig to enable scenery changes. Performances will also be capable of being transmitted across the Internet.
